## Command Details

```text
Register Control Band detectors, record deterministic Findings, derive
and triage Trigger Proposals, complete fixes, and roll up (F054 T1-T4).
A detector is a versioned, model-independent Control Band definition —
metric, source, numeric baseline, closed comparator rules (ge|gt|le|lt,
last matching rule wins), evaluation window, scope, cooldown, observation
ceiling, and the one permitted output type (finding) — registered as a
human-approved governance mutation behind a single-use committed Decision.
`detect` is target-read-only: it evaluates one declared observation
fixture against the registered definition; an in-band verdict appends
nothing, and an out-of-band verdict appends one immutable Finding
carrying the detector version, input and baseline hashes, the tier
verdict, and a stable fingerprint (subject + rule version + scope +
window). `propose` derives one immutable Trigger Proposal from one
recorded Finding — never from caller input, structurally never a
canonical artifact: repeats inside the detector's cooldown append the
Finding onto the open proposal instead of duplicating it, and outside
cooldown the open proposal must be triaged before a new one may open.
`triage` binds one open proposal to one committed human Decision under
the closed vocabulary fix|schedule|dismiss: schedule and dismiss
preserve their reasons and close the proposal reviewably, and only fix
returns a CANDIDATE Intent admission payload that must still pass the
normal canonical artifact surface — nothing is auto-admitted. Triage
Decisions are single-use across the maintain ledgers. Staleness is
derived at read time, never edited: findings and proposals read stale
when a newer detector version registers or a later observation
re-presents the fingerprint with different input. `complete` binds a
fix-triaged proposal to committed intent + eval + eval-result pins
(unresolved references refuse), so a shipped fix becomes a regression
signal. `rollup` aggregates counts by tier, status, and staleness
within a declared --limit and marks truncation explicitly. All ledgers
are hash-chained and fail every read closed.

Subcommands:
  register-detector --id <detector-id> --detector-version <v> --metric <name>
        --source <origin> --baseline <number> --rule <tier>:<ge|gt|le|lt>:<threshold>
        [--rule ...] --window-ms <n> --scope <scope> --cooldown-ms <n>
        --max-observations <n> --decision-identity <identity> --revision <n>
  detect --id <detector-id> --detector-version <v> --subject <subject>
        --window-from <iso> --window-to <iso> --value <number>
        --observation-hash <sha256:...>
  propose --finding-index <n>
  triage --fingerprint <sha256:...> --outcome <fix|schedule|dismiss>
        [--reason <text>] --decision-identity <identity> --revision <n>
  complete --fingerprint <sha256:...> --intent <identity>@<rev>
        --eval <identity>@<rev> --eval-result <identity>@<rev>
  rollup --limit <n>
  detectors
  findings [--id <detector-id>] [--fingerprint <sha256:...>]
  proposals [--fingerprint <sha256:...>]

Examples:
  amber maintain register-detector --target . --id detector/error-rate --detector-version 1 --metric http-5xx-rate --source observability/api --baseline 10 --rule warn:ge:100 --rule page:ge:500 --window-ms 3600000 --scope service/api --cooldown-ms 3600000 --max-observations 100 --owner alice@example.com --policy policy/error-budget@1 --decision-identity decision/detector-error-rate --revision 1 --json
  amber maintain detect --target . --id detector/error-rate --detector-version 1 --subject service/api --window-from 2026-08-29T00:00:00.000Z --window-to 2026-08-29T01:00:00.000Z --value 120 --observation-hash sha256:<64-hex> --json
  amber maintain propose --target . --finding-index 0 --json
  amber maintain triage --target . --fingerprint sha256:<64-hex> --outcome schedule --reason "next sprint" --decision-identity decision/triage-1 --revision 1 --json
  amber maintain complete --target . --fingerprint sha256:<64-hex> --intent intent/maintain-x@1 --eval eval/maintain-check@1 --eval-result eval-result/maintain-check-run@1 --json
  amber maintain rollup --target . --limit 100 --json
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess` and `governance report` reject output destinations that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink or junction outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- A planned output file that shares its bytes with another name — a hard link, or a link to one — is refused before the write by `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess --output-dir` and `governance report --output`, even when both names stay inside the target. A link to a single in-target file is still written through, so it replaces that file's bytes.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
